findings.claim: writeInstallEnv (install_windows.go:139-149), called from runInstall (line 97) with the raw -addr/-peek-port/-peek-control-port flag values, never reads any pre-existing install.env before writing — it always overwrites install.env with whatever the current flags resolve to (the hardcoded defaults 127.0.0.1:6001 / 4242 / 42442 unless the invoker re-passes custom values, cmd/configserver/main.go:34,51-52). Spec correctness-115 requires: 're-running the install with no overrides must preserve a profile's previously resolved values rather than resetting them to shared defaults.' The macOS counterpart (install.sh) explicitly implements this preserve-on-reinstall semantics by sourcing the existing install.env first (ENV_CONFIGSERVER_PORT/ENV_PEEK_PORT/ENV_PEEK_CONTROL_PORT, falling back to env vars, falling back to the hardcoded defaults) before writing a new one; install_windows.go has no equivalent read-before-write step anywhere in runInstall or writeInstallEnv.
findings.fix: In writeInstallEnv (or before calling it), read the existing install.env first (mirroring install.sh's ENV_CONFIGSERVER_PORT/ENV_PEEK_PORT/ENV_PEEK_CONTROL_PORT fallback chain) and only fall back to the passed-in flag defaults when no prior value exists, so a reinstall without explicit overrides preserves the profile's previously resolved ports.
findings.evidence: Re-read cmd/configserver/install_windows.go lines 72-149 and cmd/configserver/main.go lines 28-67 and 116-118 in full via git show at head 1f725cedc5c8b092c8a3d7e408793ef72840ec7e: confirmed addr/peekPort/peekControlPort flow straight from flag.String/flag.Int defaults (hardcoded literals) through runInstall into writeInstallEnv with no intervening read of install.env. Cross-checked install.sh (not in this chunk but read for comparison) at lines 6-21, which sources install.env first (`. "$REPO_DIR/install.env"`) before resolving ADDR_PORT/PEEK_PORT/PEEK_CONTROL_PORT — confirming the intended pattern this Windows path is missing. The claim survives: for any profile that has customized its ports (the entire premise of the multi-profile-ports feature), a re-run of `configserver.exe -install` without re-specifying the same -addr/-peek-port/-peek-control-port flags silently resets install.env (and therefore the plist/task port wiring and the {{PEEK_CONTROL_PORT}} expansion sync_settings.sh performs) back to the shared defaults, which is exactly the collision scenario this feature set exists to prevent.

findings.claim: startPeek's reuse check (main.go:245-258) decodes a peekID struct that includes ControlPort (line 220) from the running instance's /healthz response, but the match condition at line 248 (`id.ClaudeHome == claudeHome && id.CodexHome == codexHome`) never compares id.ControlPort against the currently-configured controlPort. Spec correctness-110 requires the identity check to expose 'the home directories and ports it is actually serving' and to reuse 'only on an exact match,' otherwise log a loud error and disable the integration. As written, a pre-existing peek-mcp process with the same claude-home/codex-home but a different (e.g. stale, pre-reconfiguration) control port is silently treated as 'already serving ... for this profile' and reused, while the caller's dashboardURL (main.go:124-126) is built from the newly-configured *peekControlPort flag — producing a dashboard link that points at a port the reused process is not actually listening its control UI on.
findings.fix: Add `&& id.ControlPort == controlPort` (or 0-vs-0 handling for a disabled dashboard) to the match condition at main.go:248 so a control-port mismatch is treated the same as a home-dir mismatch — logged loudly and the integration disabled rather than silently reused.
findings.evidence: Re-read cmd/configserver/main.go lines 216-281 in full at head 1f725cedc5c8b092c8a3d7e408793ef72840ec7e. Confirmed peekID has a ControlPort field (decoded from JSON, line 220), confirmed it is never referenced again anywhere in the file after being decoded in peekIdentity (lines 223-238), and confirmed the sole reuse-match condition at line 248 checks only ClaudeHome/CodexHome. The claim survives: the main port match is implicit (healthz was dialed on that exact port), but the control-port dimension named in the struct and the spec's 'ports it is actually serving' is collected and then dropped, so a stale listener from before a control-port reconfiguration passes the identity check and a wrong dashboard URL is handed to the operator.
